      Stored in this browser. Join the leaderboard above to also keep your last 10 games online.
    

    
      Blunder deck
      
      
        
        Train
      
      Every mistake and blunder from your games becomes a puzzle: find the move you missed. Positions return on a spaced schedule (1, 3, 7, 16, 35, 70 days), sooner when you miss them again. Each puzzle is tagged with its tactical theme.
    

    
      Endgame gym
      
      Classic endgames against full-strength Stockfish. It defends and punishes perfectly, so a pass here means you really own the technique.
    

    
      Memory gym
      
      
        Train
        
          Relaxed pace
          Standard pace
          Quick pace
        
      
      Look at a position, then rebuild it from memory, spot what changed, or answer questions about it. Positions come from your own games and the classics, never random scatter, so you train yourself to see chess patterns instead of dots. 100 stages from 4 pieces to a full board; look time scales with the piece count and shrinks as you climb, and you can always hide the pieces early when you are ready.
    

    
      Pairs
      
      
        
        
          12 cards (easy)
          16 cards
          24 cards
        
        Play
      
      The classic memory game, chess flavored. Flip two cards; a match stays up, a miss turns back over. Fewer attempts earn more stars, and each flavor teaches something real: pieces, coordinates, moves, values, mating patterns, openings, and the great players.
    

    
      Sparring
      
        
        Play themed game
        
          Knight odds
          Rook odds
          Queen odds
        
        Play odds game
      
      Themed games start from a chosen opening and count as normal games. In odds games the selected opponent starts without a piece; those are casual and stay out of your record.
    

    
      Career ladder
      
      
    

    
      Guess the move
      
       Guess for both sides (harder): predict every single move of the game
      Replay a classic game, or one of your own, and predict every move for one side. 3 points for the game move; Stockfish scores your alternatives. Each tile keeps your best finished score: green from 75%, red below 33%, yellow in between.
    

    
      Golden rules
      
      Practice the rules: one-move puzzles
      The dos and don’ts every player should absorb, phase by phase. Where a rule has a famous proof, the link opens the exact game or drill that demonstrates it.
    

    
      Opening repertoire
      
      
        Add White line
        Add Black line
        Train
      
      Record your opening lines by playing both sides on the board, then drill them from memory on the same spaced schedule as the blunder deck.
    

    
      Your opening tree
      
      
      
        Practice from here
      
      Built from your saved games. Click a move to follow the branch; the score bar shows your results, and ⚠ marks branches where they start dropping.
    

    
      Analysis board
      Open analysis board
      Free analysis with the full engine: top three lines live, move pieces for either side, set up any position, and play it out against the selected opponent.
